With its neatly lined wooden houses, its parks, and its sprawling shopping areas, Staten Island looks more like a peaceful American suburb than the image most people have of New York. It's a distinction nurtured by its residents, many of whom, driven by a nagging sense of abandonment and a fresh hostility toward the new Democratic mayor, Zohran Mamdani, go so far as to push for secession. Connected to the rest of the megacity by a single bridge and a (free) ferry, the island, part of New York since 1898, has no subway, no municipal public hospital, and few cultural institutions, lists Pat Salmon, a local historian, in comments to AFP. Until 2001, the area took in all of New York's waste in a vast landfill, now covered. (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

articles.image_title: Hapag-Lloyd: Hapag-Lloyd and other shipping containers stacked up in the port of Jebel Ali on the 29th of December 2024 in Dubai United Arab Emirates. Jebel Ali is run by DP World and is the world's ninth busiest port, the largest man-made harbour, and the biggest and by far the busiest port in the Middle-East.
